title: The world is experiencing a string of abnormally hot days—and records are being shattered
summary: We're becoming used to seeing records being broken whenever we look at data telling us about Earth's climate. Whether it's the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, heat in the ocean or shrinking sea ice around the poles, the signs of human-caused climate change are all around us.

title: Strawberries, cucumbers and lemon basil show promise for future moon and Mars menus
summary: As NASA prepares for future missions to the moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving.

title: Is AI‑assisted thinking devaluing business degrees?
summary: As AI models improve, high-quality knowledge is becoming easier to access. A degree therefore has to certify something more durable than the ability to retrieve knowledge or produce a plausible answer. It must show that a student can exercise judgment, make decisions and defend them.

title: Melting Barents Sea ice gives Eastern Europe's farmers a spring boost
summary: For decades, sea ice in the Barents Sea, a part of the Arctic Ocean north of Norway and Russia, has been shrinking as the Arctic warms. The loss of so much ice can alter weather patterns well beyond the polar region, including in Europe. But how these changes might affect vegetation growth and agricultural production is less well understood.

title: Once logging stops, recovery of Vietnam's tropical forests isn't guaranteed
summary: Deep in the jungle of central Vietnam, the heat is heavy, the mosquitoes are relentless and the terrain offers no easy paths. My colleagues and I don't hike on clear trails; we wade up riverbeds, stepping carefully over slippery rocks to access the thousands of trees we have been measuring for the last decade.

title: Hera reveals stadium-sized asteroid crater from spacecraft impact
summary: Arriving at the site of humankind's first planetary defense experiment, the European Space Agency's Hera mission has found a miniature world of surprises. Dimorphos—the small asteroid whose orbit around a second, larger asteroid was deflected by a spacecraft impact—now has one face flattened with a stadium-sized crater and is tumbling chaotically. Meanwhile, hundreds of previously unknown boulders encircle the binary pair.

title: Income inequality is rising while becoming more similar across countries
summary: Inequality is a much-debated issue in politics and society. International comparative research shows that income inequality has risen in most countries. At the same time, however, the differences in disposable income levels between countries have narrowed.

title: When bad weather hits a fragile financial system
summary: An extreme weather event does more than just destroy buildings, facilities or infrastructure. It can also reduce the value of collateral, weaken banks, make credit more expensive and force businesses to postpone investment. Consequently, the damage risks spreading well beyond the locality where the event occurred.

title: Antarctic sea ice extent hits new low
summary: Satellite observations show Antarctic sea ice coverage dipped to record daily lows in October 2026, surpassing even the extremely low extent observed in October 2023—the year poor sea ice conditions led to the deaths of thousands of emperor penguin chicks in Antarctica.

title: European oil and gas firms likely downplayed energy crisis profits, study finds
summary: Following the Russian attack on Ukraine in February 2022, energy costs rose sharply and many households and businesses felt the financial burden immediately. Oil and gas companies, however, were making extraordinary profits during this time. As public criticism of high energy costs grew, how did these companies handle their profits? A new study shows that European oil and gas firms likely downplayed their profits between 2022 and 2023. These earnings management practices were particularly prevalent in countries that introduced windfall profit taxes as well as in countries with strong democratic institutions.

title: Study shows path to more resilient future for Canada's forests
summary: Mountain pine beetles have killed millions of lodgepole pines across western North America since the 1990s, but some trees have proved more resilient than others. New research suggests part of the difference is genetic and that the resistance can be passed from one generation of trees to the next.

title: Carbon storage wells linked to earthquakes near Canadian city
summary: People across Edmonton, Canada, felt the ground shake on April 1 and again on May 9, 2026. After the May quake, the Alberta Energy Regulator said it had received no reports of damage or injuries. Researchers have now traced both earthquakes to carbon dioxide injected at Alberta's Quest storage project.

title: Artemis III Astronaut Andre Douglas Visits VAB
summary: NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, Artemis III mission specialist, stands inside an RS-25 engine test article during a visit to the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026.

title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
summary: NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency.

title: The narwhal’s legendary “unicorn horn” holds a remarkable engineering secret
summary: The narwhal’s iconic spiral tusk, once prized in Europe as the horn of a mythical unicorn, conceals an extraordinary feat of natural engineering.

title: Scientists turn one of the world’s hardest-to-recycle plastics into high-performance lubricating oil
summary: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil.

title: The Moon Watchers
summary: On November 24, all denizens of our fair planet could watch the Moon rise opposite the setting Sun. Easy to spot in twilight skies above fields, fences, backyards, and even stone walls, the Moon was big and bright, and at its…

title: Shivelyuch Socked In
summary: A cloud layer encircled the flanks of the volcano on the Kamchatka Peninsula but left its restless summit caldera in view

title: Scientists identify two ages when children may be most vulnerable to screen time
summary: Scientists have identified two potentially critical periods when screen time may be especially detrimental to children's learning and memory: infancy and the start of formal schooling.

title: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean
summary: The deep sea has long been considered a safe haven for marine life, but new genetic research suggests a hidden biodiversity crisis may be unfolding far beneath the waves.

title: These bizarre prehistoric mammals may have been misunderstood for 150 years
summary: Giant horned mammals that emerged shortly after the extinction of the dinosaurs may have had far fewer physical differences between males and females than scientists once believed.

title: For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work
summary: A major new study challenges a long-standing assumption about how the brain works, revealing that most neurons are versatile multitaskers rather than highly specialized workers.

title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China

title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
summary: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time
